technical_hypothesis.primary_training_data_risk: historical demand and handling-time series are distorted by policy changes, migrations, backlog-clearing campaigns, outages, staffing decisions and post-hoc queue edits, creating leakage and unstable seasonality

training_data.observation_unit: one queue-skill-time interval at the planning cutoff
training_data.input_data: pre-cutoff arrivals, backlog age, case type, channel, calendar, service time, skill coverage, planned absences, known campaigns and system availability; completeness across functions is unknown
training_data.target_or_reward: future arrivals and workload, followed by a deterministic objective balancing SLA risk, backlog, overtime, skill coverage and schedule stability
training_data.label_source: ticket, case, workflow, schedule and queue events; consistency between systems is unknown
training_data.prediction_time: before weekly or intraday staffing and allocation decisions
training_data.expected_volume: unknown and organization-dependent; low-volume specialist queues may be too sparse for local models
training_data.class_balance: not directly applicable to forecasting; peaks and severe backlog events are expected to be rare and uneven
training_data.historical_coverage: unknown; mature shared-service and ITSM platforms may retain several years, while migrations and taxonomy changes can break comparability
training_data.train_validation_split: rolling time-based validation with holdouts spanning policy, system and organizational changes; queue or business-unit grouped tests where transfer is claimed
training_data.leakage_risks: using final resolved category, revised priority, completed handling time, later staffing changes, backlog-clearing actions or incident severity unavailable at planning time
training_data.representativeness_risks: business unit, channel, skill taxonomy, automation level, labor rules, hybrid work, policy changes and system maturity vary materially
training_data.feedback_loop: staffing and routing decisions alter future backlog, handling time and observed demand, so forecasts trained on prior policies can reinforce under-service of difficult queues
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: employee schedules and case metadata require minimization, role-based access and LGPD controls; productivity prediction must not become opaque individual performance scoring
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: use seasonal baselines, Erlang or queueing formulas where applicable, configured calendars, capacity thresholds, deterministic skill constraints and manager-adjusted scenarios

portfolio_comparison.reason: Demand forecasting plus constrained capacity allocation is already represented in sector-specific opportunities. Cross-industry shared-service planning does not introduce a distinct data modality, authority boundary, intelligent mechanism or measurable outcome, and mature workforce-optimization products already cover demand scenarios, schedules, skills and queues.

existing_landscape.summary: Adopt or configure workforce-optimization and service-management capabilities, normalize queue and skill taxonomies, and begin with seasonal or queueing baselines plus deterministic constraints. Train local forecasts only when historical stability and incremental value over built-in forecasting are demonstrated.

research.findings: Current Brazilian official statistics confirm the scale and continued growth of services, but do not expose a uniquely cross-industry forecasting gap. Current workforce-optimization products already model demand scenarios, staffing impact, schedules, skills, queues and surge coverage. The remaining work is primarily adoption, data normalization and deterministic constraint configuration rather than a differentiated opportunity.
